finding: The interviews do not establish that expanding police-medic scope improves survival, safety, response time or clinical outcomes.
This report alone does not prove that FOCUS caused mental-health improvement, is superior to alternatives, or would work similarly in Brazilian security organizations.
The protocol does not establish that BBTI is non-inferior, improves access, or produces clinical or implementation benefit.
The study does not prove that any single intervention component caused the improvement or that the same effect would occur in Brazilian tactical/public-safety systems.
The study does not directly establish mortality, shock outcomes, battlefield effectiveness or patient-level superiority of ketamine/fentanyl in actual hemorrhage.
The study does not show that the assessed capacities reduce sexual assault incidence or that GTO support will produce improved outcomes.
The review does not prove that any single implementation strategy causes improved violence outcomes or transfers directly to Brazilian public safety.
The review does not demonstrate that embedding drowning interventions in these programs reduces drowning or will be effective in another jurisdiction.
The article does not establish direct applicability to police readiness, nor a causal effect of any single intervention on mental-health or operational outcomes.
The review does not establish that a specific training package improves police performance, clinical outcomes or operational readiness.
